title: egress-opaque-error-traceback-and-replay
content:
Summary:
- Intermittent 502/524-like failures from private deployment instances to external HTTPS services (api.thirdparty.example). Failures correlate with bursty outbound traffic and long-running HTTP/2 connections.

Observed symptoms:
- Client app: repeated curl POSTs to https://api.thirdparty.example/v1/ingest returned: 
  * curl: (56) OpenSSL SSL_read: Connection was reset, errno 104
  * Later: curl: (35) SSL_connect returned=1 errno=0 state=error: certificate verify failed (when we forced SNI)
- On host (edge node in customer VPC): connections to 3rd party succeed ~90% of the time; failures cluster in 30s windows.
- tcpdump shows TLS ClientHello but no ServerHello in many failed cases; sometimes ServerHello but immediate TCP RST from remote IP.
- No application logs indicating payload issues; requests are identical across success/failure.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) NAT ephemeral port exhaustion or port reuse leading to remote server rejecting or resetting (timing matches burst windows).
2) MTU/fragmentation affecting TLS handshake extension (SNI/ALPN) or TCP MSS causing handshake stalls on larger TLS ClientHello (HTTP/2).
3) Middlebox or remote rate-limiter dropping repeated connections from same source port pair (we see similar source ports reused).
4) Route asymmetry causing SYN/SYN-ACK to traverse different path and get filtered; remote RST originates from outside our expected egress IP.

Commands tried / immediate artifacts (raw outputs trimmed):
- netstat -n -p | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l
  -> 142 (when observed failures)

- ss -tn sport = :443 state established
  -> shows many TIME_WAIT/ESTABLISHED entries, a surge of ephemeral local ports around :33400-33550

- sudo iptables -t nat -L -n -v
  -> no odd NAT rules on host; VPC NAT gateway in cloud account shows high active connections in console.

- sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max && cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
  -> 65536 && 62388 (close to saturation during peak)

- sudo conntrack -L | grep SYN_RECV | wc -l
  -> ~120 (lots of partially-open connections)

- curl -v --http2 https://api.thirdparty.example/v1/ingest -d '{"x":1}'
  * Repro on laptop vs node: laptop (home network) always succeeds. Node: sometimes succeeds, sometimes handshake fails.
  * Verbose show: TLS 1.3 ClientHello
    --> server: (no reply) or server: ServerHello then immediate TCP RST

- openssl s_client -connect api.thirdparty.example:443 -servername api.thirdparty.example -msg -state
  -> when failing: ClientHello sent, no ServerHello, then RST. When succeeding: full handshake, ALPN h2 selected.

- tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/egress-fail.pcap host api.thirdparty.example and port 443 (captured 100+ failed attempts)
  -> inspected in Wireshark: common pattern is ClientHello size 1200+ bytes (many ALPN/extension entries), segmented across 2 TCP segments; server does not ACK second segment in failing cases.

- iperf3 tests to a friendly endpoint in same region: throughput stable; MTU test: ping -M do -s 1472 <remote> -> fragmented, but 1440 works.

- traceroute to api.thirdparty.example during fail window shows 10 hops then * * * then remote IP replies with ICMP unreachable at times. Not conclusive.

- checked AWS VPC NAT metrics (customer account): NAT Gateway BytesOut and ActiveConnections spike aligning with failures. Flow logs show src ports in ephemeral range reused often.

Packet-level notes:
- Many failed ClientHello packets are 1360-1420 bytes (TLS with many extension + big SNI for long hostnames).
- In failing traces: server ACKs first 1k of the ClientHello then does not ACK subsequent segment -> retransmit -> RST.
- Hypothesis: Path MTU/CIFS-like middlebox dropping fragments or dropping GRE/fragmented packets; TCP MSS clamping wrong.

Evidence for ephemeral port exhaustion:
- NAT Gateway ActiveConnections approaches its documented soft limit for our tier (we're in a medium tier in test infra).
- When we lowered client concurrency, failures decreased.
- When we rotated source IPs via launching additional egress instances, overall success improved.

TLS-specific oddities:
- Some failures change error string to certificate verification failures when we set SNI explicitly in curl; suggests handshake aborted mid-exchange and client reports cert verify after receiving partial data from an intermediate.
- No consistent server-side 4xx/5xx in third-party logs; they see reset TCP sessions.

Definitive reproduction steps (best effort):
1) From edge node, run this script to simulate burst: for i in {1..400}; do curl -sS -k -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" --http2 https://api.thirdparty.example/v1/ingest -d '{"batch":1}' & sleep 0.02; done; wait
2) Watch conntrack, netstat, and NAT Gateway metrics.
3) tcpdump on egress IP (host) during run, then analyze pcap.

Quick mitigation tried and result:
- Reduced client concurrency (throttle) -> success rate improves.
- Switched to a different egress IP (spin ephemeral instance behind a different NAT) -> success improves.
- Forced TLS 1.2 (curl --tlsv1.2) -> marginal improvement; fewer large ClientHello sizes.
- Enabled HTTP/1.1 instead of HTTP/2 -> handshake size smaller -> fewer failures.

Open questions / TODO:
- Is the NAT gateway doing any TCP MSS clamping or fragment reassembly that could cause ACKs to drop? (check cloud provider docs & open support ticket).
- Are there intermediate firewalls doing deep packet inspection and resetting when they see repeated client port reuse?
- Can we get packet captures on the cloud provider egress device (support request)?
- Is conntrack table size adequate for steady-state? Should we increase nf_conntrack_max on nodes (test change) or add connection pooling?

Short-term action plan (next 48h):
- (Ava) Implement client-side backpressure: limit concurrency from 200 -> 50 and add exponential backoff for 5xx/connection errors. (ETA: 2025-10-09)
- (Rory) Open cloud support ticket for NAT gateway behavior and ask for packet capture on provider-side (include PCAP and timestamps). (ETA: 2025-10-07)
- (Maya) Run controlled experiments: vary TLS version, ALPN, and hostname length to observe which extension triggers failures. (ETA: 2025-10-08)
- (Ops) Increase nf_conntrack_max on a test node to 200k and retest, measure regression of failures. (ETA: 2025-10-10)

Longer-term ideas:
- Consider using egress pool with multiple NAT IPs to reduce per-IP connection pressure and avoid reuse collisions.
- Add connection reuse/proxy at edge: maintain long-lived upstream connections (HTTP/2 multiplexing) instead of frequent new handshakes.
- Add MTU discovery and client-side MSS clamp to avoid fragmented ClientHello.

Notes to self / freeform:
- This one felt like classic NAT exhaustion + MTU bit. The fact that forcing HTTP/1.1 or TLS1.2 helps points to large ClientHello being a factor.
- If provider confirms they do not fragment and we cannot get provider-side PCAP, raising conntrack and shuffling IPs is a pragmatic fix.
- Remember to check for any recent change to our ALPN list or inclusion of long custom extensions (we added a long x-client-id header last week?).

Immediate logs + pcap attached in ticket JIRA-PI-4821. Will paste tcpdump excerpt later.

Unresolved: who to loop in from third-party? Their ops said they saw RSTs and couldn't see payload. Might need mutual packet traces.

End of scratchpad.
